items.title: What happens if you don't put your phone in airplane mode?
items.summary: What happens on a flight if you don't put your phone in airplane mode? In the US, 5G phones use 3.7 to 3.98 GHz and the radar altimeter that measures height above the ground works at 4.2 to 4.4 GHz, a gap of 220 MHz. In Europe the phone band is 3.4 to 3.8 GHz, a gap of 400 MHz. EASA leaves it to each airline to decide whether devices can stay on. Idea: Mark Rober, his Short "What happens if you don't use Airplane mode?". Sources: FAA radio altimeter rule and the FCC Upper C-band order (Federal Register, July 31, 2026), EU Decision 2019/235, EASA. The 3D scene is a diagram, not to scale. Sound ...

items.title: llm 0.37.2
items.summary: Release: llm 0.37.2 Fixes a security issue reported by Daniel de Araujo in GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w . LLM has a mechanism called extra-openai-models.yaml - now managed by the new-in-0.37 llm openai endpoint add command - for using LLM with OpenAI-compatible API endpoints from other providers. Daniel reported two ways this could accidentally send your configured OpenAI API key to one of those providers: if the key named by api_key_name had never been stored, or if a responses: true model was run with -o chat_completions 1 . Tags: projects , security , llm , releases

items.title: Antarctica's biggest land animal is a midge
items.summary: Antarctica's biggest land animal is smaller than a grain of rice. It is a wingless midge, Belgica antarctica, at most 6 millimeters long. Larvae winter at minus 2 to minus 10 Celsius, dry out by up to about 70 percent of their body water, then freeze solid and survive down to around minus 20. Idea from Cleo Abram's Antarctica Short. Photos: Igor Gvozdovskyy and Julien Renoult (CC BY 4.0). Footage: NASA.
